standard_prerequisites.name: The henselian property is equivalent to bijectivity on idempotents for every integral algebra
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Lemma \ref{lemma-characterize-henselian-pair}, cited at proof lines 2777 and 2784 and 2792-2795
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the criterion applied to the two nested pairs and to the chain of quotient maps.

standard_prerequisites.name: The henselian property is preserved by integral ring maps
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the henselian property of the quotient pair from the larger pair.

core_obligations: Assume both smaller pairs henselian and consider an integral algebra with the chain of quotients by the two ideals (proof lines 2775-2779).
Use the criterion to see that both arrows induce bijections on idempotents, hence so does the composition, giving that the larger pair is henselian (proof lines 2780-2784).
Conversely, use the permanence result to get the quotient pair and record the bijection for the composition (proof lines 2785-2791).
Deduce that the first arrow induces a bijection on idempotents and conclude that the smaller pair is henselian (proof lines 2792-2795).
proof_roadmap: From the two smaller pairs to the larger one (proof lines 2775-2784).
From the larger pair to the quotient pair (proof lines 2785-2786).
From the composition to the smaller pair (proof lines 2787-2795).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for ideals contained in one another, the pair is henselian if and only if both the pair cut out by the smaller ideal and the pair of the quotient by the larger ideal are henselian. Both directions are proved by the same mechanism: the idempotent lifting criterion along an integral algebra, which is checked for the two maps in the chain from the algebra to its quotients by the two ideals. One direction uses that a composition of bijections on idempotents is a bijection, the other that the middle arrow of a composition and the whole composition being bijections forces the first arrow to be one, combined with the permanence of the henselian property under integral maps.
